title: Staged release quality sentinel and automated self-heal for model/config changes
creator: Priya Desai
description: Problem: model and config changes are a leading source of regressions in production quality. Current canary/A-B rollouts surface regressions slowly and require a lot of manual triage. Goal: implement an automated staged-release 'quality sentinel' that continuously evaluates a rolling sample of traffic + synthetic prompts during staged releases, computes composite signals, and enforces automatic, reversible remediation actions when regressions exceed thresholds. Non-goal: replace human decision-making for ambiguous, low-signal regressions; humans remain in the loop for policy tuning and high-risk changes.
acceptance_criteria: Quality sentinel runs for every staged release (A/B and staged ramps) and evaluates traffic-sampled and synthetic prompts within 5 minutes of variant traffic appearing.
Composite quality score computed and visible in Console per-variant: helpfulness delta, hallucination delta, toxicity delta, latency delta, cost-per-token delta.
Automated rollback or mitigation actions triggered when configured composite-thresholds are breached for a sustained window (configurable default: 3m sustained at 2x severity threshold).
Rollback action is auditable in the control plane with a reversible audit log entry and links to the triggering signals and evaluation snapshots.
Integration tests that simulate regression signal and assert controller performs configured mitigation (revert model, switch to fallback policy, or throttle traffic).
implementation_notes: Create a lightweight 'shadow-eval' mode in the evals harness to run micro-evaluations (100-500 sampled requests / minute) without impacting latency-critical path.
Composite score is a weighted aggregation: 40% task-quality (eval metrics), 25% hallucination penalty, 15% safety (toxicity/PII checks), 10% latency impact, 10% cost delta.
Add a new control-plane component 'release-gate-controller' that subscribes to rollout events, receives eval deltas, and makes deterministic decisions per policy.

Mitigation actions supported initially: auto-revert to previous model version, switch to quantized/fast variant, divert a percentage of traffic to fallback policy, or pause rollout and notify on-call.
Persist evaluation snapshots to the existing evals artifact store (immutable) and attach snapshot IDs to controller decisions for post-mortem.
Expose fine-grained policy configuration in Console (thresholds, window, severity mapping, mitigation order) and an API for programmatic overrides.
Ensure rate limits and cost caps for shadow-eval to avoid runaway billing on high-traffic rollouts.
Respect customer privacy: sampled inputs are hashed and only non-sensitive artifacts are sent to shared services; private deployments use local evals-only mode.
Instrumentation: add new metrics to prod-metrics (release_gate.composite_score, release_gate.decision, release_gate.rollback_count) and dashboard panels for per-release timelines.
Controller will create a reversible release action via the existing rollout service; rollback is performed by calling rollout API with previous pinned model-version and annotated audit message.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): implement shadow-eval harness + composite scoring and run against nightly canaries in staging (2 weeks).
Phase 2 (internal): deploy release-gate-controller to internal cluster, run against internal feature flags and staged A/B experiments (1 week).
Phase 3 (pilot): opt-in enterprise customers and a small subset of hosted traffic (5% of new releases) with monitoring-only mode (no automated rollback) for 2 weeks.
Phase 4 (gradual enable): enable automated mitigations for low-risk model changes (small config flags) with strict thresholds and human-approval cooldown for model-version changes (2 weeks).
Phase 5 (GA): open settings in Console, default to monitoring-only for new accounts, provide guardrail templates for enterprises, and run a Q2 reliability campaign to tune thresholds.
test_plan: Unit tests for composite score calculation with synthetic deltas covering edge cases (zero-traffic, noisy signals, metric inversion).
Integration test: simulate staged rollout with injected regression in hallucination metric and assert controller triggers configured mitigation within window.
E2E canary test: run shadow-eval in a test cluster with production-like traffic replay and verify audit artifacts are produced and linked.
Chaos test: simulate delayed metric ingestion and ensure controller applies conservative backoff instead of false rollback.
Performance test: ensure shadow-eval overhead is <1% compute impact on serving tier under typical workloads and cost impact is within projected budget caps.
